sources.title: 2017 leadership-campaign profile: birth date, elections and cabinet career
sources.findings: Read the 2017 Fine Gael campaign profile: birth 18 January 1979, Trinity medical qualification, 1999 unsuccessful local campaign, 2004 election, 2007 Dublin West victory and cabinet sequence from 2011. Its age 38 is date-specific, not current. Party assertions about popularity, integrity, tourism and welfare successes are campaigning claims, not independent policy evaluation. The public profile uses election years, not unsupported day-level election dates. The campaign page is not evidence of his current office.

sources.title: 14 June 2017 profile: April 2003 medical degree and 2010 GP qualification
sources.findings: Read Trinity’s 14 June 2017 report: six-year medical degree completed April 2003, junior-doctor work at St James’s and Connolly, then GP training and qualification in 2010. Do not equate 2003 graduation with GP qualification or call the clinical qualification an earned research PhD. The university reports his selection as Taoiseach that day. Its account of relatives is unnecessary to reproduce in detail; no current clinical practice or registration was verified.

sources.title: 14 June 2017 parliamentary nomination, vote and political representation
sources.findings: Read Sky’s 14 June 2017 report: parliamentary nomination received 57 for, 50 against and 45 abstentions; age 38, openly gay and son of an Indian immigrant. Youngest is explicitly at the time, avoiding a permanent record claim after Simon Harris. The article’s exactly-ten-years-since-taking-his-seat wording refers to a parliamentary sitting, not necessarily the May 2007 election day. Its ordinal description is not copied because conventions for counting repeated Taoisigh differ. Do not turn the Dail nomination into a direct popular vote for prime minister.

sources.title: 2018 termination-of-pregnancy bill memorandum: referendum and constitutional amendment dates
sources.findings: Read the opening/background of the parliamentary explanatory memorandum for the 2018 termination-of-pregnancy bill. It gives the referendum on 25 May, 66.4% Yes and 33.6% No, and constitutional amendment signed 18 September. The subsequent healthcare bill is a separate legislative step. Descriptions in an explanatory memorandum are not proof of every provision’s final commencement or immediate nationwide availability of services. The public page does not claim all restrictions were abolished on referendum day.

sources.title: 10 October 2019 Wirral meeting and possible Brexit agreement
sources.findings: Read ITV’s substantive text on the 10 October 2019 Wirral meeting, the leaders’ positive joint statement and remaining unresolved questions. Discussion of a possible agreement is not signature, ratification, actual EU departure, or final settlement of all Northern Ireland issues. The Halloween deadline in contemporary reporting was an aspiration, not the later actual exit date. The video was not watched, and no claim is made that Varadkar alone negotiated the EU–UK agreement.

sources.title: 27 June 2020 actual appointment of Micheal Martin
sources.findings: Read the President’s retrospective entry confirming actual appointment of Micheal Martin on 27 June 2020, warrant and seal under Article 13. This establishes the interruption between Varadkar’s two premierships, rather than treating an earlier election or an announcement as the handover. Site navigation naming the current president does not alter the historical Michael D. Higgins event.

sources.title: 7 July 2020 record of 27 June ministerial appointments and initial department names
sources.findings: Read the appointment announcement in the 7 July 2020 official Dail record. Martin reports the appointments took place on 27 June and assigns Varadkar the Tanaiste role and the Department of Business, Enterprise and Innovation pending department/function changes. The parliamentary reporting date is not the appointment date. Preserve the initial department name rather than projecting the later Enterprise, Trade and Employment name backward as an unchanged legal title. No full review of the entire sitting or all subsequent transfer orders is claimed.

sources.title: 17 December 2022 actual reappointment of Varadkar as Taoiseach
sources.findings: Read the presidential entry confirming that Higgins actually signed the warrant and presented the seals to Varadkar on 17 December 2022. Earlier plans specifying 15 December, or the November announcement agreeing 17 December, are not actual accession. A coalition rotation is distinct from a new national election. The exact evening sequence of all other ministers is unnecessary and omitted.

sources.title: 6 July 2022 police-confirmed decision not to prosecute over GP contract disclosure
sources.findings: Read The Journal’s July 2022 report including the Garda statement that the DPP directed no prosecution against any individual in the investigation into the 2019 GP-contract disclosure. The same report notes acknowledgment of sending the document and earlier parliamentary controversy. Do not retain an allegation as a conviction, describe the decision as a court acquittal, or silently convert Varadkar’s own claims about opponents and innocence into a judicial finding. No confidential prosecutorial reasoning or original investigation file was reviewed.

sources.title: 20 March 2024 resignation announcement, housing pressure and referendum defeats
sources.findings: Read Reuters’ 20 March 2024 announcement report: personal/political reasons attributed to Varadkar; planned succession without an automatic general election; housing pressure, post-pandemic recovery and referendum defeat. Announcement is not the formal April resignation or a July decision on reelection. Campaign predictions, bookmaker odds and the then-latest possible election deadline are not current facts. Broad assessments of recovery are not a standalone causal economic audit, and his public coming-out during the 2015 campaign is not an inferred private characteristic.

sources.title: 8 April 2024 formal resignation accepted by President Higgins
sources.findings: Read the President’s entry for 8 April 2024, 18:00: Higgins accepted Varadkar’s resignation. This is the formal resignation event, separate from the 20 March announcement and 9 April appointment of Harris. The entry itself does not set out the complete constitutional caretaker mechanism, so no detailed legal interpretation is invented.

sources.title: 9 April 2024 appointment of Simon Harris as Taoiseach
sources.findings: Read the President’s 9 April 2024 entry: Higgins signed the appointment warrant and presented the Taoiseach/Government seals to Simon Harris. This verifies completed succession rather than relying on an earlier scheduled parliamentary vote. Current site navigation and the historical event’s president are kept separate.

sources.title: 16 July 2024 announcement that he would not seek reelection
sources.findings: Read the opening and relevant announcement paragraphs of The Irish Times’ 16 July 2024 report. Varadkar announced at a Fine Gael constituency meeting that he would not contest the next general election, giving prospective nominees preparation time. This future decision is not immediate resignation of his existing TD seat and is separate from April departure as Taoiseach. Later Irish News reporting confirms he had left elected politics in 2024; public text does not assert an unverified day of parliamentary departure.

sources.title: Speaking My Mind: publisher biography and 11 September 2025 ebook publication
sources.findings: Read Penguin’s book description, author biography and edition details for ISBN 9781405978200, showing ebook publication 11 September 2025 and separate 2025 hardback/2026 paperback links. Do not confuse a paperback reissue with first publication, bestseller advertising with independently audited sales, or award shortlist with victory. The book itself was not read; no detailed historical claim is verified solely by promotional praise or autobiographical assertions.

sources.title: 16 November 2026 published interview on Irish unity, culture and post-office politics
sources.findings: Read the substantive opening of the 16 November 2026 Irish News interview: completed conversation, post-office status, still Fine Gael member, Irish-unity advocacy, north–south attitudes and cultural identity. Publication date is not a verified recording date. The 2022 file-photo caption is not the date of the new interview. Personal hopes, referendum polling, Orange Order predictions and assessments of identity are not established future outcomes or government commitments. No recording viewed and no claim to have read the complete underlying unity blueprint.

sources.title: 27 June 2020 coalition ministerial appointments and planned December 2022 rotation
sources.findings: Read the short Reuters report via Devdiscourse dated 27 June 2020. It records Martin’s government appointments, Varadkar’s deputy-premier/enterprise remit, and a planned December 2022 return under the coalition agreement. The planned return is confirmed by the later presidential actual-appointment record. Contemporary journalistic use of the future department title is distinguished from the initial legal assignment in the parliamentary record.

sources.title: 8 March 2024 family and care referendum overview and rejection
sources.findings: Read the Electoral Commission’s family-and-care overview opening: two separate constitutional votes held 8 March 2024, family concept and family care, and rejection. It is an independent explanatory institution, not an advocate of Varadkar’s proposals. Public text omits vote percentages, since the separate long commission report did not expose matching final-result text in the sections read. Policy defeat is not itself proof of one exclusive cause for his later resignation.
